```{r all-severity-levels}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ranger)
library(pROC)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load Data & Prepare Binary Target Variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Loading and preparing dataset...\n")

raw_accidents <- read_csv(
  "US_Accidents_March23_sampled_500k.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 100000) %>%
  mutate(
    # Parse Timestamps & Calculate Duration Target (Minutes)
    Start_Time = parse_date_time(Start_Time, orders = c("ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd"), tz = "UTC"),
    End_Time   = parse_date_time(End_Time, orders = c("ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd"), tz = "UTC"),
    Duration_mins = as.numeric(difftime(End_Time, Start_Time, units = "mins")),
    
    # Define Binary Target (Factor with valid R variable names)
    Duration_Category = factor(
      if_else(Duration_mins >= 120, "Over_2_Hours", "Under_2_Hours"),
      levels = c("Under_2_Hours", "Over_2_Hours")
    ),
    
    # Feature Engineering
    Hour = hour(Start_Time),
    Day_of_Week = wday(Start_Time, label = TRUE),
    Is_Rush_Hour = factor(if_else(Hour %in% c(7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18), "Yes", "No")),
    
    # Predictors
    Temperature = `Temperature(F)`,
    Humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    Visibility = `Visibility(mi)`,
    Precipitation = coalesce(`Precipitation(in)`, 0),
    Distance = `Distance(mi)`,
    Severity_factor = factor(Severity),
    
    # Categorical Variables
    State = fct_lump_n(factor(State), n = 15),
    Junction = factor(Junction),
    Traffic_Signal = factor(Traffic_Signal),
    Crossing = factor(Crossing)
  ) %>%
  # Remove clear duration outlier records
  filter(Duration_mins >= 2 & Duration_mins <= 1440)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Dataset Setup
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dataset 1: Full Dataset (Includes Severity)
data_full <- raw_accidents %>%
  select(
    Duration_Category, Severity_factor, Hour, Day_of_Week, Is_Rush_Hour, 
    State, Distance, Temperature, Humidity, Visibility, Precipitation,
    Junction, Traffic_Signal, Crossing
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

# Dataset 2: Severity 2 Crashes Only
data_sev2 <- raw_accidents %>%
  filter(Severity == 2) %>%
  select(
    Duration_Category, Hour, Day_of_Week, Is_Rush_Hour, 
    State, Distance, Temperature, Humidity, Visibility, Precipitation,
    Junction, Traffic_Signal, Crossing
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Train / Test Splits (80/20 Stratified)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
train_idx_1 <- sample(seq_len(nrow(data_full)), size = 0.8 * nrow(data_full))
train_full  <- data_full[train_idx_1, ]
test_full   <- data_full[-train_idx_1, ]

train_idx_2 <- sample(seq_len(nrow(data_sev2)), size = 0.8 * nrow(data_sev2))
train_sev2  <- data_sev2[train_idx_2, ]
test_sev2   <- data_sev2[-train_idx_2, ]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Train Both Binary Random Forest Classifiers
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Training Model 1 (All Crashes with Severity Factor)...\n")
fit_rf_model1 <- ranger(
  formula = Duration_Category ~ .,
  data = train_full,
  num.trees = 300,
  probability = TRUE,     # Return class probabilities for ROC/AUC
  importance = "impurity",
  seed = 42
)

cat("Training Model 2 (Severity Level 2 Subset Only)...\n")
fit_rf_model2 <- ranger(
  formula = Duration_Category ~ .,
  data = train_sev2,
  num.trees = 300,
  probability = TRUE,     # Return class probabilities for ROC/AUC
  importance = "impurity",
  seed = 42
)

cat("Both binary models trained successfully!\n\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Evaluate Performance & Compute Binary Classification Metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
evaluate_binary_rf <- function(model_obj, test_data, model_name) {
  # Predict probabilities
  prob_preds <- predict(model_obj, data = test_data)$predictions[, "Over_2_Hours"]
  actual_class <- test_data$Duration_Category
  
  # Predicted class at 0.5 threshold
  pred_class <- factor(
    if_else(prob_preds >= 0.5, "Over_2_Hours", "Under_2_Hours"),
    levels = c("Under_2_Hours", "Over_2_Hours")
  )
  
  # Compute ROC and metrics
  roc_obj  <- roc(actual_class, prob_preds, levels = c("Under_2_Hours", "Over_2_Hours"), quiet = TRUE)
  auc_val  <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  
  cm <- table(Actual = actual_class, Predicted = pred_class)
  
  tp <- cm["Over_2_Hours", "Over_2_Hours"]
  tn <- cm["Under_2_Hours", "Under_2_Hours"]
  fp <- cm["Under_2_Hours", "Over_2_Hours"]
  fn <- cm["Over_2_Hours", "Under_2_Hours"]
  
  acc <- (tp + tn) / sum(cm)
  sens <- tp / (tp + fn)  # True Positive Rate (Recall)
  spec <- tn / (tn + fp)  # True Negative Rate
  
  list(
    metrics = tibble(
      Model = model_name,
      `Test Sample` = nrow(test_data),
      `ROC-AUC` = round(auc_val, 4),
      `Accuracy` = paste0(round(acc * 100, 2), "%"),
      `Sensitivity (Recall)` = paste0(round(sens * 100, 2), "%"),
      `Specificity` = paste0(round(spec * 100, 2), "%")
    ),
    roc = roc_obj
  )
}

res1 <- evaluate_binary_rf(fit_rf_model1, test_full, "Model 1: All Crashes (+ Severity)")
res2 <- evaluate_binary_rf(fit_rf_model2, test_sev2, "Model 2: Severity 2 Only")

cat("=================================================================================\n")
cat("            BINARY CLASSIFICATION COMPARISON: OVER/UNDER 2 HOURS                 \n")
cat("=================================================================================\n")
print(knitr::kable(bind_rows(res1$metrics, res2$metrics), align = "lccccc"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot ROC Curves Side-by-Side Comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
roc_df1 <- tibble(
  fpr = 1 - res1$roc$specificities,
  tpr = res1$roc$sensitivities,
  Model = paste0("Model 1: All Crashes (AUC = ", sprintf("%.3f", res1$roc$auc), ")")
)

roc_df2 <- tibble(
  fpr = 1 - res2$roc$specificities,
  tpr = res2$roc$sensitivities,
  Model = paste0("Model 2: Severity 2 Only (AUC = ", sprintf("%.3f", res2$roc$auc), ")")
)

bind_rows(roc_df1, roc_df2) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, color = Model)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2b5c8f", "#2e8b57")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curve Comparison: Binary Crash Duration Models",
    subtitle = "Predicting long-duration crashes (Over 2 Hours)",
    x = "False Positive Rate (1 - Specificity)",
    y = "True Positive Rate (Sensitivity)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Extract Feature Importances & Compute Relative Percentages
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
get_binary_importance_df <- function(model_obj, model_label) {
  tibble(
    Predictor = names(model_obj$variable.importance),
    Importance = model_obj$variable.importance,
    Model = model_label
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Normalize values to total 100% relative importance
      Rel_Importance = (Importance / sum(Importance)) * 100
    )
}

# Combine importance metrics from both binary classification models
importance_binary_combined <- bind_rows(
  get_binary_importance_df(fit_rf_model1, "Model 1: All Crashes (+ Severity)"),
  get_binary_importance_df(fit_rf_model2, "Model 2: Severity 2 Subset Only")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Plot Side-by-Side Relative Feature Importance Graphs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use facets so the comparison only depends on ggplot2.
combined_importance_plot <- importance_binary_combined %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = reorder(Predictor, Rel_Importance),
      y = Rel_Importance,
      fill = Model
    )
  ) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Rel_Importance)),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "gray20"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Model 1: All Crashes (+ Severity)" = "#2b5c8f",
      "Model 2: Severity 2 Subset Only" = "#2e8b57"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Binary Random Forest Feature Importance Comparison",
    subtitle = "Gini impurity reduction across 300 classification trees per model",
    x = "Predictor Variable",
    y = "Relative Importance (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

print(combined_importance_plot)
```
